source_snapshot.procedure: Install the AMD hpl.tar.bz2 package on Ubuntu 20.04 or newer with internet/root access; run versioned install and configuration generators; execute run_hpl_ccx.sh with AMD CCX-specific behavior.
source_snapshot.criteria: The result should match with Intel/AMD spec.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: After the AMD HPL package is installed, run the benchmark and return N, NB, P, Q, time, and Gflops for comparison.

original_test_intent.purpose: Measure CPU double-precision dense linear-system performance with a platform-appropriate HPL build and configuration, validate numerical completion, and compare the result with an approved comparable vendor reference.
original_test_intent.target: The approved CPU server SUT, including its CPU/NUMA/cache topology, host DDR, firmware, OS, compiler/math/MPI stack, and power/thermal profile.
original_test_intent.scope: The source procedure is specifically AMD HPL/CCX-oriented, while the acceptance criterion names Intel or AMD; vendor and platform must be selected before a runnable profile is defined.
original_test_intent.operation: Install or stage an approved platform-specific HPL package, generate/approve HPL.dat and process/thread placement for the exact topology, run under monitoring, and capture validated performance output.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The source gives 360 machine minutes but no explicit number of measured runs, warmups, aggregation rule, or fixed HPL problem matrix.
original_test_intent.expected_result: HPL completes its numerical validation and the reported Gflop/s meets the owner-provided baseline under demonstrably comparable hardware, software, tuning, and run conditions.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Vendor/SKU/topology, package checksum/version, build and dependency provenance, generated HPL.dat and placement files, exact command, N/NB/P/Q, runtime, Gflop/s, residual/pass status, telemetry/throttling/errors, repetition rule, and reference provenance/configuration.
ambiguities: No CPU vendor/SKU or approved Intel/AMD baseline and tolerance is supplied.
The procedure's AMD versioned scripts and fixed eight-threads-per-CCX description are not universal across AMD generations and do not define an Intel path.
The source does not define whether 360 minutes is a time budget, benchmark duration, or repeated-run window.
source_conflicts: The Common case provides an AMD-only install/run procedure but accepts against an unspecified Intel/AMD specification.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly treats the package, root/network access, generated CPU-specific files, monitoring, and baseline as prerequisites rather than permanent blocks. It does not elevate the AMD-only procedure versus Intel/AMD criterion mismatch to SOURCE_CONFLICT and retains source script examples before a vendor/SKU is selected.

applicable_history.decision: Stress/benchmark duration, topology, package, tuning, and acceptance baselines must be preserved and supplied; missing packages or references are readiness inputs, not automatic BLOCKED.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The benchmark is automatable after setup, but no universal command is valid: the case must first bind to AMD or Intel, an exact CPU/SUT configuration, an approved HPL distribution/profile, repetitions, and a comparable acceptance baseline. V3 does not apply the AMD CCX scripts to Intel or newer AMD platforms by assumption.

available_now: HPL CPU-performance intent, high-load nature, expected core metrics, and AMD source workflow are identifiable.
Read-only topology, BIOS/power profile, OS/toolchain inventory, thermal/error baselines, and package inspection can occur before a benchmark is authorized.
missing_inputs: CPU vendor/SKU/socket/NUMA/cache topology and explicit selection of AMD or Intel execution path
Approved HPL distribution/build, checksum/license, supported OS/toolchain/MPI/BLAS, generated configuration method, root/network policy, and package compatibility
HPL problem configuration, binding/SMT/power profile, warmup/measured-run count, 360-minute interpretation, aggregation rule, abort thresholds, and maintenance approval
Comparable reference result with source, exact configuration, metric/tolerance, and required numerical residual/validation status
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The performance owner selects vendor-specific package/profile, run matrix, and baseline; the lab/security owner approves root/network/package installation, high-load window, limits, and recovery.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect CPU/NUMA/cache/core/SMT/memory topology, firmware/OS, current governor/power state, idle telemetry, and pre-existing kernel/BMC events
Inspect and hash the supplied archive and scripts, enumerate dependencies and outbound downloads, and compare their stated supported platforms without executing as root
prohibited_until_closed: Do not run AMD CCX scripts on an Intel target, assume source versioned scripts fit a different AMD generation, execute unreviewed root/network installers, clear logs, or alter SMT/governor/BIOS/power settings
Do not compare Gflop/s across unmatched configurations, omit residual validation, or declare PASS from Gflop/s alone
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner signs one vendor/SKU-specific immutable run profile and comparable baseline; scripts/package are reviewed and hashed; the SUT is isolated, limits and abort/recovery are tested, and run/repetition semantics fit the 360-minute requirement.

revision_candidate.purpose: Run a validated, vendor-appropriate HPL profile on the approved CPU SUT and compare repeatable, numerically valid Gflop/s with a configuration-matched reference.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: One explicitly selected Intel or AMD CPU server configuration with approved firmware/OS, host memory, compiler, BLAS, MPI, HPL distribution, cooling/power profile, and maintenance window.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Host CPU and DDR performance for the selected SUT. AMD CCX/CCD scripts apply only when the supplied AMD package and exact EPYC generation support them; they are not an Intel path.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Vendor/SKU/topology, approved HPL package/checksum/license and supported stack, HPL.dat/process/thread/binding/SMT profile, installation permissions, measured-run count and 360-minute meaning, telemetry limits, comparable reference configuration/result/tolerance, and recovery owner.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Review and install or stage the approved vendor-specific package; generate and preserve topology-specific HPL files; verify N/NB/P/Q, memory use, process/thread placement and residual checking; run the approved measured matrix under monitoring; retain every output and exact profile. Use the source AMD scripts only when their named package/version matches the selected AMD SUT.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Dedicated SUT, configuration-matched baseline, verified archive/scripts/dependencies, approved root/network activity, sufficient memory/storage/cooling/power, stable idle baseline, synchronized evidence collection, and tested abort/OOB path.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Full identity/configuration, package/build provenance, generated HPL.dat and placement, run/repetition timestamps, N/NB/P/Q/time/Gflop/s, numerical residual/pass output, CPU/memory/thermal/power/throttle/error telemetry, reference provenance, per-run comparison, and restored state.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The owner-approved Intel or AMD result for the same CPU/socket/memory/firmware/software/tuning profile, with a defined metric, tolerance, repetition/aggregation rule, and mandatory HPL numerical validation.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No unreviewed root installer or outbound dependency, production workload, log clearing, silent topology/tuning change, cross-vendor script reuse, or continuation beyond approved thermal/power/error limits.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Approval is required for package/network/root installation, SUT tuning, sustained load, run matrix, baseline comparability, limits, and any reboot or recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Engineering supplies and approves vendor profile and reference; after setup, generation, execution, monitoring, evidence capture, and calculation are automatable. Final comparability exceptions remain an engineering judgment.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop HPL cleanly, preserve partial output and health logs, terminate MPI/workers, restore approved SMT/governor/power/profile changes, verify hardware/OS health, and do not rerun an invalid or throttled profile without review.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Vendor/profile mismatch, unsupported or untrusted package/script, invalid generated topology, insufficient memory/cooling/power, active workload, numerical residual failure, thermal/power/throttle/error threshold, instability, incomplete run/evidence, or incomparable baseline.

identified_defects: The source combines AMD-only scripts and CCX assumptions with a vendor-neutral Intel/AMD criterion.
No comparable reference, tolerance, repetitions, or interpretation of the 360-minute machine time is supplied.
Fixed eight-thread/CCX guidance is generation-dependent and cannot be generalized.
A performance value without HPL numerical validation and configuration provenance is insufficient for acceptance.
reason_for_change: Prevent cross-vendor or cross-generation script reuse and make reproducibility, numerical validity, and baseline comparability part of completion rather than treating any Gflop/s output as a result.

new_technical_evidence.title: AOCL User Guide 5.3: Running the HPL Benchmark
new_technical_evidence.applicability: AMD EPYC; configuration differs by generation/SKU
new_technical_evidence.supports: MPI ranks, L3/CCX/CCD mapping, and OpenMP thread counts vary with the specific EPYC generation and SKU.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The case does not identify an AMD CPU generation or even confirm AMD as the target.

new_technical_evidence.title: HPL Tuning
new_technical_evidence.supports: HPL.dat parameters materially affect the run and the residual test is part of determining validity; performance output alone is not sufficient.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The approved HPL parameters and threshold for this SUT are absent.

removed_ambiguities: Requires vendor selection before any command is chosen.
Makes repetitions, 360-minute meaning, numerical validity, and matched baseline explicit.
Separates AMD generation-specific examples from universal HPL intent.
resolved_blockers: A missing tarball, compiler stack, or baseline is treated as a supplyable readiness condition, not an intrinsic automation block.
remaining_blockers: Execution and final acceptance remain pending vendor/SKU binding, package/profile compatibility, approved run matrix, safety limits, and a comparable reference.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 identifies the cross-vendor source conflict V2 left implicit, prevents AMD CCX scripts from being treated as a Common/Intel path, and defines reproducibility and residual validation as mandatory evidence while retaining V2's package, approval, monitoring, and recovery gates.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source installs AMD HPL versioned scripts and runs one instance per CCX, yet its criterion says Intel/AMD spec.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 retains AMD examples while asking for a generic vendor baseline; V3 requires vendor/SKU selection before defining commands.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: No root/network installer or high-load run until package/profile and comparable baseline are approved; preserve residual, placement, telemetry, and recovery evidence.
